$comment: CV-3801 overland belt conveyor twin. Expected drive power, tensions, slip and take-up position are computed in Maximo Monitor from the design data (ISO 5048 method); the device sends only what it measures.

identification.model: Steelcord ST2000, 1200 mm, RS covers 10 + 6 mm
identification.description: Overland ore conveyor, primary crusher to stockpile: 2.5 km, +40 m lift, 2 x 560 kW head drive
identification.belt: Fenner Dunlop Steelcord ST2000 steel cord belt, 1200 mm wide, RS covers (DIN W / ISO D abrasion class) 10 mm top, 6 mm bottom
identification.drive: Head drive: one rubber-lagged drive pulley (1000 mm), two 560 kW motors with gearboxes and VFDs (master / follower torque sharing)
identification.takeup: Gravity take-up with 22 t counterweight on the slack side, just after the drive
identification.idlers: Three-roll 30 degree carrying idlers every 1.2 m, single-roll return idlers every 3.0 m
identification.monitoring: Belt weigher, non-driven pulley speed encoder, take-up load pins and position, belt tracking sensors at head and tail, fixed idler thermal scanners, steel cord belt scanner

route.source: Plant layout of the conveyor (centre distance and lift): assumption: typical value, replace with your conveyor design report / supplier data

belt.source: Fenner Dunlop Steelcord datasheet (fennerdunlopemea.com, steelcord-en.pdf): strength, cord diameter and pitch, carcass weight, minimum pulley diameters and the rule belt mass = carcass + 1.15 x cover thickness (mm). Cover thicknesses 10 + 6 mm and the belt stiffness (force per unit strain, from 0.25 % elastic elongation at 10 % of the breaking strength): assumption: typical value, replace with your conveyor design report / supplier data

idlers.source: Rotating mass of the idler rolls per metre (3 x 6.5 kg carrying rolls every 1.2 m, 15 kg return roll every 3.0 m): assumption: typical value, replace with your conveyor design report / supplier data

resistance.source: ISO 5048:1989 clause 5.1.3: basic artificial friction coefficient f = 0.02 (three-roll 30 degree idlers, 108-159 mm rolls, about 5 m/s, 70-110 % load, about 20 C); clause 5.1.2: C = (L + L0) / L with L0 between 70 and 100 m (85 m taken).

material.source: Crushed ore, loose bulk density and design capacity: assumption: typical value, replace with your conveyor design report / supplier data

drive.source: ISO 5048:1989: eta1 between 0.85 and 0.95 (0.92 taken), mu = 0.35 for rubber lagging with herringbone grooves in clean and wet conditions (Table 4), wrap angle in the 160-240 degree range. Motor rating, belt speed and pulley size: assumption: typical value, replace with your conveyor design report / supplier data

takeup.source: Gravity take-up: counterweight mass, available carriage travel and the carriage position with the new belt at standstill (x0): assumption: typical value, replace with your conveyor design report / supplier data

demo.note: Demo only: the feed from the crusher wanders between 2050 and 2400 t/h; the plant clock runs in real time and the readings do not depend on the time of day.

points.label: Belt speed at a non-driven pulley
Drive pulley surface speed (from motor speed)
Belt off-centre at the head (+ = right)
Belt off-centre at the tail (+ = right)
Hottest idler in the last thermal scan
Idlers more than 20 K above ambient
Largest splice length growth since installation
Number of the splice with the largest growth
Cord damage indications in the last scan
Thinnest top cover in the last thickness survey

limits.source: Alert limits: assumption: typical value, replace with your conveyor design report / supplier data. Splice growth and cover limits must come from the belt supplier and the splicing contractor.

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

high_resistance.name: High running resistance (spillage, build-up, cold, sticky idlers)
high_resistance.symptoms: drive power above the ISO 5048 expectation at the same tonnage; apparent friction factor up

idler_bearing_failure.name: Idler bearing failure
idler_bearing_failure.symptoms: one idler hot on the thermal scan, then very hot (fire risk)

lagging_wear.name: Drive pulley lagging worn or wet and dirty
lagging_wear.symptoms: belt slips on the drive pulley with normal take-up tension

takeup_jammed.name: Take-up carriage jammed
takeup_jammed.symptoms: take-up force low, slack-side tension below the Euler-Eytelwein minimum, then slip

belt_stretch.name: Permanent belt elongation (stretch)
belt_stretch.symptoms: take-up carriage creeps to the end of its travel

splice_failure.name: Steel cord splice deterioration
splice_failure.symptoms: belt scanner shows one splice getting longer

mistracking.name: Belt mistracking (misalignment)
mistracking.symptoms: belt runs off centre at the tail, power a little up

load_share_imbalance.name: Motor load sharing lost
load_share_imbalance.symptoms: one motor carries most of the load and goes over its rating
